results.caption: #ad Canning up some Hamburger Dill Pickles that will last us all year, full recipe from the 38th Edition @ballcanning Blue Book Guide to Preserving below! <3 #BallHomeCanningAmbassador   I’ve had so much fun recently learning to can with Ball® Home Canning, and I can’t believe how delicious these pickles turned out. They were so simple too!!! Such a good way to use up the surplus of summer cucumbers. Also, I’m obsessed with these cute star jars, I’ve linked them in my bio in my ShopMy (in the “kitchen” section) if you want to get them too. Who else is learning how to can this year? Hamburger Dills Recipe Yield: about 7 pint jars  Ingredients -4 pounds 4-to 6-inch cucumbers -6 tablespoons salt for canning and pickling -1 quart plus ½ cup water -1 quart white vinegar, 5% acidity -14 heads fresh dill -3½ teaspoons mustard seed -14 black peppercorns -Ball Pickle Crisp (optional) Instructions 1. PREP Wash cucumbers under cold running water; drain. Remove stem and 1/16 inch from blossom end of cucumbers. Cut cucumbers crosswise or lengthwise into ¼-inch slices. 2. COOK Combine salt, water, and vinegar in a large saucepan. Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to a simmer; simmer 10 minutes. 3. FILL Pack cucumbers into a hot jar, leaving ½-inch headspace. Put 2 heads of dill, ½ teaspoon mustard seed, and 2 peppercorns in jar. Add ⅛ teaspoon Pickle Crisp to pint jar, if desired. Ladle hot pickling liquid over cucumbers, leaving ½-inch headspace. 4. Remove air bubbles. Clean jar rim. Center lid on jar and adjust band to fingertip-tight. Place jar on the rack in boiling-water canner with simmering water (180°F). Repeat until all jars are filled. 5. PROCESS Water must cover jars by 1 inch. Adjust heat to medium-high, cover canner, and bring water to a rolling boil. Process pint jars 15 minutes, adjusting for altitude Turn off heat and remove cover. Let jars cool 5 minutes. Remove jars from canner: do not retighten bands if loose. Cool 12 to 24 hours. Check seals. Label and store jars. Enjoy!!! Ball® and Ball logotype TMs Ball Corporation, used under license. #summercanning #summerrecipes #homemadepickles

results.transcript: Today we're making pickles to last all year long with the makers of Ball Home Canning. I have so many sweet memories hanging out in the kitchen as a kid while my mom and grandma canned summer produce. And now I'm finally learning how to do it on my own. Today we're making hamburger dills which is a perfect way to turn your summer cucumbers into something that will last. And they're absolutely delicious on a juicy summer burger. The recipe I'm using is from the 38th edition Ball Blue Book Guide to Preserving which is full of both classic and unique recipes. All tested and approved for safety. Today we are water bath canning which is a very beginner friendly canning method. I'll put the full recipe in the caption if you want to try these. Happy summer canning and cheers to learning something new.

results.caption:
I finally got every car guy’s dream: a lift! 

DONT WORRY, THE VIDEOS WILL CONTINUE TO BE ON JACK AMD JACK STANDS WITH COMMON HAND TOOLS!!!!

If you ever wanted a lift, here is a quick overview of things to consider and how the lift is installed. The big things to consider is having enough space for the lift, making sure your concrete is thick enough, and finally running the electric.

When you work on cars outside, in your driveway, on jack stands almost every day for 10yrs, this is a dream come true! I got a new @bendpak 10AP lift that I will use OFF CAMERA to maintain my fleet of project cars. 

#ChrisFix

results.transcript: Hey guys, Chris Fix here. I just bought a house, which means I now have my own garage. And as you can see, this floor is a mess. So in the last video, I showed you how to epoxy coat it, so it went from this to this. And now it's looking absolutely amazing. So for this video, I want to show you how to install something anyone who works on cars dreams of owning. A lift. And the first thing you need to do is figure out what lift you want. You could get a four-post lift or a two-post lift, but if you don't have high ceilings, you could also get a scissor lift or a short two-post lift like this. But I'm going with a two-post 10AP that could lift 10,000 pounds. Now before you go buy a lift, you need to check the specifications to make sure your concrete is safe for the lift. And you can see here, it says the concrete needs to be at least 4.25 inches thick and be rated at least 3,000 PSI. And figuring that out is easy. Just contact your town's permit records department, and they could give you the plans for your house. And you can see right here, it says it's 5 inches thick and 3,000 PSI, so we're good to go. You also want to make sure you have enough space, at least 145 inches high and 145 inches wide. And that's not a problem in my garage. Now you can install this lift with a couple of buddies, but since this is my first lift, an installation company is showing me how it's done. The first step is to get both of these heavy lift posts in place. And I'm really thankful they're being extra careful with my new floor. Then once the two posts are squared to each other, you could get the top support bar bolted in, and then now the lift could be bolted to the ground. So first you have to drill the holes out using a masonry bit, and it's a good idea to use a vacuum to keep the concrete dust to a minimum. Then you want to get all that dust and broken concrete out of the hole, that way there's no obstruction for the bolt that goes in there. Now these are special concrete anchor bolts, and they have to get hammered into the hole. Now before we tighten down the bolts all the way, it's important that each of these posts on the lift is level. And you can see here, ours is a little out of spec. It's not bad. So all we need to do is add a couple thin shims under the base plate, and check it out, now it's perfectly level. So with it level, now the bolts could be torqued to spec, which is 90 foot-pounds. Then, after all the bolts are tightened down, the lift arms are installed, and hydraulic fluid is added to the reservoir. But there's one more thing left to do, and that's to run the electric to the lift. And they're going to add a new circuit breaker, in this case a two- pole 20 amp, and that'll feed 220 volts at a max of 20 amps to the lift. Then the wire is run up the conduit, up the wall, and it comes all the way across here, down the lift, and it's finally connected to this control box right here. So a couple more splices into the control box and we're done. And after about five hours of work, the lift is ready to try out for the first time. So you just have to press this button, and that's all there is to it. Now each clank you hear is the automatic safety stops, and then once you're at the top, you just press this lever down to drop it onto the safety stop, and check it out. This is amazing. Now I can work on my car so much easier, but don't worry, my videos will always be done in a driveway with common hand tools.
